clue.text: Cop's plants are flops

blocks.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, so the cop's is DI'S
asters are daisy-like garden flowers

explanation.surface: A police officer's garden has failed miserably.
explanation.definitionFit: A flop is a total failure, the same as a disaster, both plural nouns here.

clue.text: Sleepy? Yes, but not that particular little chap!

definitions.text: Sleepy? Yes, but not that particular little chap!

blocks.note: surface reading: a question about drowsiness
setter's reading: Sleepy is one of Snow White's seven dwarfs, but the answer is a different one whose name also means drowsy

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone is drowsy, then pointedly ruling out the well-known dwarf of that name.
explanation.walkthrough: Two of the seven dwarfs in Snow White have names meaning drowsy; the clue wants the other one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means drowsy or stupefied, and is also the name of another of the seven dwarfs.

clue.text: Not hearing rock, fade out

indicators.note: out suggests being put out of order, so the preceding word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a rock is a stone
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot hear rock music as it fades away.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely unable to perceive sound; the idiom describes total loss of hearing.

clue.text: He maligns society, country and Queen without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece sits around the other

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for society
a country is a land
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
er is the sound made while hesitating

explanation.surface: A critic attacks society, the nation and the monarch without pausing for breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without hesitation' reads as 'promptly', but 'without' means outside here; the two ER pieces nest.
explanation.definitionFit: A slanderer is a person who speaks falsely to damage someone's reputation, i.e. one who maligns.

clue.text: With surprising completion of sentence, income tax malarky's not entirely problematic

indicators.note: not entirely means the last word is used without its final letter
problematic suggests something troubled and in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Complaining that tax bureaucracy is troublesome nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the front and is itself a cryptic description: the punctuation that ends a sentence with surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation symbol closes a sentence expressing astonishment, so it completes a surprised sentence.

clue.text: Ruling oneself out from splendid life is beginning of chastity

indicators.note: out suggests disorder, so the following letters are shaken into a new order
beginning of keeps only the first letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
its first letter

explanation.surface: A moralist suggesting that self-control starts with chastity rather than a splendid life.
explanation.definitionFit: Being able to control one's own conduct and impulses is governing, or ruling, oneself.

clue.text: Pick off insects from budgie I lost when moving

indicators.note: lost means that letter goes missing from the bird's name
moving means the remaining letters shift position

blocks.note: taken as written
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: Removing parasites from a pet budgerigar after it lost them in a move.
explanation.definitionFit: To debug literally means to remove bugs, which are insects, so picking them off fits.

clue.text: Pan-American League?

blocks.note: first meaning: a large cooking pot or mess tin used by soldiers and campers
second meaning: the name for the southern US states that formed the Confederacy

explanation.surface: Looks like the name of an international sports competition spanning the Americas.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'Pan-American' joins two separate definitions; the question mark flags the Confederacy as a kind of league.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an army cooking pot and also the American South, the Confederate states once allied together.

clue.text: Players ask cabbie to move up a bit

indicators.note: a bit means only a portion of the run of letters is taken
in a down clue, moving up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: letters lying across the two words

explanation.surface: Team members request that a taxi driver pull forward a little.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, rugby and hockey the defensive players are called by this collective name.

clue.text: Start to gather ancient cane plant

indicators.note: start to keeps only the opening letter of the next word

blocks.note: its first letter
olden means of old times
a cane is a rod

explanation.surface: Instructions to begin collecting an old walking cane or sugar plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cane plant' looks like one phrase, sugar cane; the definition is just the final word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tall perennial with yellow flower spikes, a common garden and wild species.

clue.text: Girl in snap is pedestrian

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a snap is a photo, a pic
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman in a photograph turns out to be walking on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedestrian' looks like a noun for someone walking; it is the adjective meaning dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian as an adjective means dull and uninspired, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Content of telex, I calculate, is concerning Collins, perhaps?

indicators.note: content of means the letters are found inside the words that follow

blocks.note: letters running across these words

explanation.surface: Estimating that a telex message relates to a person called Collins.
explanation.walkthrough: Collins is a publisher of English dictionaries, so something to do with Collins, perhaps, relates to words.
explanation.definitionFit: Lexical means relating to words or vocabulary, the subject matter of a dictionary such as Collins.

clue.text: Return amateur work about the French volte-face

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece encloses the other
a volte-face is an about-turn, so the whole result is turned back to front

blocks.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is home improvement done by an amateur
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An amateur project that turns around a French matter yields a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A return on an investment is its yield, the income it produces.

clue.text: He gets a letter of notice and violently sees red

indicators.note: violently suggests the words being smashed about into a new order

blocks.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man receives a warning letter and flies into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: The addressee is the person to whom mail is directed, so he is the recipient.

clue.text: Lance spelling "attention"?

blocks.note: sp is the abbreviation for spelling, as in a proofreader's mark
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Someone called Lance spells out the word attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lance' looks like a man's name; it is the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long pointed weapon for thrusting, essentially a synonym.

clue.text: Out cold and unable to hear, perhaps?

blocks.note: first meaning: unconscious
second meaning, read literally: lacking a sense, deafness being one example

explanation.surface: Someone knocked unconscious who therefore cannot hear anything.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means unconscious, and taken literally means without one of the five senses, such as hearing.

clue.text: One joining rebels Sam mobilised

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Sam rallies a band of insurgents and one of them signs up.
explanation.definitionFit: An assembler is one who fits or puts parts together, i.e. one who joins them.

clue.text: Encrypted new mail encloses abridged regulation concerning drugs

indicators.note: encrypted means scrambled into code, so the letters are reordered
encloses means the scrambled letters go around the other piece
abridged means shortened, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written
an edict is an official order

explanation.surface: A coded message contains a shortened rule about pharmaceuticals.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicinal means having healing properties or relating to medicine, i.e. to drugs.

clue.text: "Vim" toilet concoction — a recurring theme (for Rumpole, etc?)

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters are blended into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; Vim is a brand of scouring cleaner
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Rumpole of the Bailey, the TV barrister, has stock phrases such as calling his wife 'She Who Must Be Obeyed', hence recurring themes.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotiv is a recurrent musical or literary motif associated with a character or idea.

clue.text: Two objects official sent back to Nebraska for old queen

blocks.note: NE is the postal abbreviation for Nebraska
it is a pronoun used as an object, twice
a ref, referee, is a match official

explanation.surface: An official returns a pair of items to Nebraska in place of an ancient monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefertiti was an Egyptian queen of the 14th century BC, wife of Akhenaten.

clue.text: Forgot words and exited holding Richard's head

indicators.note: holding means one piece goes around the other
the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: to exit is a euphemism for dying
its first letter

explanation.surface: An actor forgets his lines and leaves the stage carrying Richard's head, as in a history play.
explanation.walkthrough: In theatre, an actor who dries forgets the lines; the surface's stage picture conceals that.
explanation.definitionFit: In acting slang, to dry is to forget one's lines, so the past tense fits forgot words.

clue.text: Touching proposal during dinner, perhaps — starter forgotten!

starter forgotten means the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: dinner is an example of a meal
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like the first course of the dinner; it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Touching means stirring the feelings, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Regard retained by well-to-do Uruguayan

blocks.note: letters running across these words

explanation.surface: Esteem kept up by a wealthy South American.
explanation.definitionFit: Odour can mean reputation or standing, as in being in good odour with someone, so it means regard.

clue.text: Maybe Madeira's topping, but freezing!

blocks.note: first meaning: the sugary coating on a cake such as Madeira
second meaning: forming ice

explanation.surface: Madeira, the sunny island, may be top-notch but it is cold.

clue.text: Desert transport arrived a bit late

blocks.note: came means arrived
its first letter

clue.text: Poles out of bounds?

blocks.note: taken as written

clue.text: Foreign objects crunched in Cox I ate

taken as written

clue.text: Tease German passions with essential wear for diplomats?

blocks.note: to kid is to tease

explanation.surface: Teasing German enthusiasms while dressing the part of a diplomat.
